data.turoyo: Balki u mede, d kətle, kule kəmzabanle d qodər, d mʔamən u darbo, d oṯe l harke. Kməftakər, mə d maṭi l harke, lə kʕuyazle tə mede, i ḥkume gədmrabyole.
data.translation: Perhaps he sells everything he has so that he can secure the journey and come here. He thinks that when he arrives here he will need nothing at all; the government will feed him.

rationale: Thin Infectum/1 gains a connected 3sg experiencer -le with negative zero-marked tə mede stimulus, contrasting the inherited first-person examples.

summary: All four candidates concern need or lack and are relevant to the lexical family, but none securely supplies an absent verbal form box. No examples, new senses or stem changes are proposed from uncertain categories.

PrS 15/80 has latyo ʕyuz with a monetary expression. PrS 53/16 has Latno ʕoyuz, while PrS 68/25 has plural Latna with invariant ʕawəz. These independent negative-copula constructions contrast with the finite forms in the existing entry and cannot automatically be assigned to Preterit Intransitive, Infectum or Part act.

63/342 predicates absence of u mede ʕoyuzo with aʕli. This does not establish a new finite construction with an affected participant; the word may be a lexical modifier rather than a verbal predicate.
The reader reports dictionary adjective variants. That report supports caution but is not treated as a newly verified dictionary fact. No claim of a missing glossary form rests on it.

The Arabic etymology and the entry's established qaṭəl-shaped Preterit Intransitive and l-suffixed Infectum examples are retained without normalizing the distinct surface forms ʕyuz, ʕoyuz, ʕawəz and ʕoyuzo.
kʕuyazle has the overt experiencer -le and a negative indefinite needed theme; no Detransitive morphology is established by English need.

ʕuyazwo has -wo but no overt experiencer suffix or named needed item. The input's food and groom-family arguments are contextual proposals, absent from the supplied verse; do not publish them as observed arguments.

Retain the Preterit Intransitive versus l-suffixed Infectum distinction and the round-1 questions about lexical adjectives. The new finite evidence does not license adding a Part act. or Infinitiv box.
Identify the grammatical category and paradigm of ʕyuz (PrS 15/80): productive Infinitiv, lexical noun, or adjective?
Is ʕoyuz in Latno ʕoyuz dinore a lexical adjective, a Part act., or an uninflected Infectum predicate? Obtain agreement contrasts.
Why is ʕawəz invariant with plural Latna in PrS 68/25? Verify whether the construction has a fixed adjective rather than a finite Preterit Intransitive.
In 63/342, does ʕoyuzo mean 'needed', 'lacking', or 'in need'? Clarify its relation to mede and aʕli before any lexical or argument-structure proposal.

Jan 2.8/1977: is suffixless ʕuyazwo an impersonal necessity construction, an omitted l-experiencer, or an active subject-needed form? Recover the antecedent of saymiwo before selecting it as a self-contained example.
Jan kʕuyazle tə mede supports the inherited l-suffixed Infectum experiencer pattern. It does not resolve the nominal/adjectival ʕyuz/ʕoyuz cases left open in round 1.
